objective: I can practice noticing body signals. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Across one regular day at home, the learner carries a small card divided into four boxes labeled hunger, thirst, tiredness, and bathroom need, and makes a tally mark in a box each time that signal shows up, without judging whether the timing was convenient.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l01-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l01-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l01-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l01-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Describe one specific moment today when you noticed a signal and what you were doing right before you noticed it, such as playing outside, reading, or sitting still.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u04-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Signal noticing: Tallies land in at least three of the four boxes across the day. | Neutral naming: The four neutral signal names are used consistently for every tally. | Reflection specificity: The reflection names a specific signal and the activity happening right before it. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner repeat the same four-box tally on a different kind of day and compare, in writing, which signal showed up in a different order between the two days.

resources.title: noticing body signals coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Across one regular day at home, the learner carries a small card divided into four boxes labeled hunger, thirst, tiredness, and bathroom need, and makes a tally mark in a box each time that signal shows up, without judging whether the timing was convenient.
Coach direction: Before you start tallying, make a guess about today.
Learner prompt: Guess which of the four signals (hunger, thirst, tiredness, bathroom need) you think you will notice the most times today, and explain why you picked it.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: noticing body signals complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Every time you notice one of the four signals today, make a tally mark in that box right away.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I made a tally mark within a few minutes of noticing the signal, not at the end of the day from memory.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I used one of the four neutral signal names (hungry, thirsty, tired, need a bathroom break) instead of a mood word like grumpy or bored.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I noticed and tallied at least three separate signal moments today.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I tallied a signal in the box that matched it, not in whichever box was closest.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: noticing body signals minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Describe one specific moment today when you noticed a signal and what you were doing right before you noticed it, such as playing outside, reading, or sitting still.

Success checks: Signal noticing: Tallies land in at least three of the four boxes across the day. | Neutral naming: The four neutral signal names are used consistently for every tally. | Reflection specificity: The reflection names a specific signal and the activity happening right before it.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: noticing body signals supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u04-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional noticing body signals condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Signal noticing: Tallies land in at least three of the four boxes across the day. | Neutral naming: The four neutral signal names are used consistently for every tally. | Reflection specificity: The reflection names a specific signal and the activity happening right before it..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.

safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
